fernand-braudel.name: Fernand Braudel
fernand-braudel.summary: French historian (1902–1985) of the Annales School whose scholarship emphasized large-scale socioeconomic history, including works on the Mediterranean and on civilization and capitalism.

francesco-i-de-medici.name: Francesco I de' Medici
francesco-i-de-medici.summary: Second Grand Duke of Tuscany, ruling from 1574 until his death in 1587, and a member of the House of Medici.

galata.name: Galata
galata.summary: A historic district on Istanbul's Golden Horn, a Genoese colony from 1273 to 1453 and home to the 1348 Galata Tower; now part of the Beyoğlu quarter.

ogier-ghiselin-de-busbecq.name: Ogier Ghiselin de Busbecq
ogier-ghiselin-de-busbecq.summary: A 16th-century Flemish diplomat and writer who served as ambassador to the Ottoman Empire and is credited with introducing tulips to Western Europe.

mamluk.name: Mamluks
mamluk.summary: Non-Arab enslaved soldiers, often of Turkic or Circassian origin, who converted to Islam and trained for war before being freed to serve as an elite military and political class in Egypt for nearly 1,000 years.

ercole-i-d-este.name: Ercole I d'Este
ercole-i-d-este.summary: Duke of Ferrara, Modena, and Reggio from 1471 until his death in 1505, known for patronizing the arts and strengthening his duchy's economy and political standing.

lady-mary-wortley-montagu.name: Lady Mary Wortley Montagu
lady-mary-wortley-montagu.summary: English aristocrat and writer, 1689 to 1762, who lived in Ottoman Constantinople as an ambassador's wife and is credited with introducing smallpox inoculation to Britain.

ottoman-mamluk-war-1516-1517.name: Ottoman–Mamluk War (1516–1517)
ottoman-mamluk-war-1516-1517.summary: The conflict in which the Ottoman Empire defeated the Mamluk Sultanate, gaining the Levant, Egypt and the Hejaz and transforming into a vast empire spanning the Islamic world.

evliya-elebi.name: Evliya Çelebi
evliya-elebi.summary: Ottoman Turkish explorer (1611–1684) who spent over 40 years traveling through the Ottoman Empire and neighboring lands, recording his journeys in a travelogue called the Seyahatname.

suleiman-the-magnificent.name: Suleiman the Magnificent
suleiman-the-magnificent.summary: Ottoman sultan from 1520 to 1566, whose long reign brought the empire's greatest economic, military and political power and reformed its legal system.

mimar-sinan.name: Mimar Sinan
mimar-sinan.summary: Chief Ottoman architect, engineer and mathematician (c. 1488/1490–1588) under sultans Suleiman the Magnificent, Selim II and Murad III, credited with over 300 structures including the Selimiye Mosque.

ehzade-mosque.name: Şehzade Mosque
ehzade-mosque.summary: A 16th-century Ottoman imperial mosque in Istanbul, commissioned by Suleiman the Magnificent as a memorial to his son Şehzade Mehmed and one of architect Mimar Sinan's earliest major works.

s-leymaniye-mosque.name: Süleymaniye Mosque
s-leymaniye-mosque.summary: An Ottoman imperial mosque in Istanbul commissioned by Suleiman the Magnificent and designed by architect Mimar Sinan, completed around 1557 and considered a masterpiece of Ottoman architecture.

transylvanian-rugs.name: Transylvanian rugs
transylvanian-rugs.summary: A term for Islamic and Oriental carpets, many of Anatolian Ottoman origin, imported to or made in Transylvania from the 15th century onward and now preserved mostly in Hungarian churches there.

k-lliye.name: Külliye
k-lliye.summary: A complex of buildings centered on a mosque in Turkish architecture, often including a madrasa, clinic, kitchens, bakery and hammam, funded by a charitable foundation.

imaret.name: Imaret
imaret.summary: A public soup kitchen built across the Ottoman Empire from the 14th to 19th centuries, often part of a larger complex with mosques and hospices, giving free food to the needy.

sabil-fountain.name: Sabil
sabil-fountain.summary: A small kiosk in Islamic architecture where water was freely dispensed to the public, common in Ottoman and Mamluk cities.

caravanserai.name: Caravanserai
caravanserai.summary: A roadside or urban inn common across the Islamic world that sheltered travelers, merchants and pack animals along trade routes such as the Silk Road.

bayezid-ii-mosque-istanbul.name: Bayezid II Mosque
bayezid-ii-mosque-istanbul.summary: An early 16th-century Ottoman imperial mosque complex in Istanbul, built near the ruins of the ancient Forum of Theodosius.

r-stem-pasha-mosque.name: Rüstem Pasha Mosque
r-stem-pasha-mosque.summary: An Ottoman mosque in Istanbul designed by imperial architect Mimar Sinan and completed around 1563, noted for its extensive İznik tile decoration.

iznik-pottery.name: Iznik pottery
iznik-pottery.summary: A decorated ceramic ware made in the Anatolian town of İznik from the late 15th to late 17th century, originally inspired by Chinese blue-and-white porcelain but developed into a distinct Ottoman style.

mahmud-i.name: Mahmud I
mahmud-i.summary: Sultan of the Ottoman Empire from 1730 to 1754, known as "the Hunchback", whose reign saw wars in Persia and conflicts in Europe while he wrote poetry.

nuruosmaniye-mosque.name: Nuruosmaniye Mosque
nuruosmaniye-mosque.summary: Designed by the Greek architect Simeon Kalfa, this mosque has one of the largest domes in Istanbul and anchors a larger religious complex near the Grand Bazaar.

ottoman-baroque-architecture.name: Ottoman Baroque architecture
ottoman-baroque-architecture.summary: An 18th- and early 19th-century Ottoman architectural style influenced by European Baroque, begun under Mahmud I with the Nuruosmaniye Mosque of 1755.

davud-agha.name: Davud Agha
davud-agha.summary: Chief imperial architect of the Ottoman Empire from 1588 until 1598 or 1599, succeeding Sinan.

murad-iii.name: Murad III
murad-iii.summary: Ottoman sultan from 1574 to 1595 whose reign saw wars with the Habsburgs and Safavids, briefly made Morocco a vassal, and included patronage of illustrated manuscripts.

tughra.name: Tughra
tughra.summary: Calligraphic monogram or seal of an Ottoman sultan, affixed to official documents and coins, with a unique design for each ruler.

hilya.name: Hilya
hilya.summary: An Ottoman art form and literary genre describing the physical appearance of Muhammad, rendered in fine calligraphy and sometimes carried as a protective amulet.

cornelis-de-vos.name: Cornelis de Vos
cornelis-de-vos.summary: Flemish painter (1584-1651) and one of Antwerp's leading portraitists, known especially for sensitive portraits of children and families, and a regular collaborator with Rubens.

portrait-of-abraham-grapheus.name: Portrait of Abraham Grapheus
portrait-of-abraham-grapheus.summary: A 1620 oil painting by Cornelis de Vos depicting a fellow member of Antwerp's painters' guild, now in the Royal Museum of Fine Arts, Antwerp.

pieter-de-hooch.name: Pieter de Hooch
pieter-de-hooch.summary: Dutch Golden Age painter (baptized 1629, died after 1679) famous for quiet domestic genre scenes, a contemporary of Vermeer in Delft's painters' guild.

tulip-period.name: Tulip Period
tulip-period.summary: A relatively peaceful era in Ottoman history, 1718 to 1730, named for a court craze for tulips and marked by a revival of art and architecture with new Western influences.

battle-of-chaldiran.name: Battle of Chaldiran
battle-of-chaldiran.summary: A 1514 battle in which the Ottoman Empire decisively defeated the Safavids, letting the Ottomans seize Eastern Anatolia and Upper Mesopotamia and halting further Safavid expansion westward.

ismail-i.name: Ismail I
ismail-i.summary: Founder and first shah of Safavid Iran, ruling from 1501 to 1524, who unified Iran under native rule and made Twelver Shia Islam the state religion, before being defeated by the Ottomans at Chaldiran in 1514.

ottoman-safavid-war-1532-1555.name: Ottoman–Safavid War (1532–1555)
ottoman-safavid-war-1532-1555.summary: A conflict between Suleiman the Magnificent's Ottoman Empire and Tahmasp I's Safavid Empire, ending with Ottoman territorial gains confirmed by the Peace of Amasya.

peace-of-amasya.name: Peace of Amasya
peace-of-amasya.summary: An 1555 treaty between Safavid Iran and the Ottoman Empire that ended their 1532 to 1555 war, dividing the Caucasus between the two powers.

russian-conquest-of-the-caucasus.name: Russian conquest of the Caucasus
russian-conquest-of-the-caucasus.summary: The Russian Empire's conquest of the Caucasus mainly between 1800 and 1864, fought against local rulers as well as the Ottoman Empire and Qajar Iran.

abbas-the-great.name: Abbas the Great
abbas-the-great.summary: Fifth Safavid shah of Iran, ruling 1588-1629 and widely considered the dynasty's greatest ruler, who brought the empire to its military, political and economic height.

gilan-province.name: Gilan province
gilan-province.summary: A province in northwestern Iran along the Caspian Sea, whose capital is the city of Rasht.

mazandaran-province.name: Mazandaran
mazandaran-province.summary: An Iranian province on the southern Caspian coast, spanning forests, plains and the Alborz mountains including Mount Damavand, known for agriculture, fish farming and tourism.

new-julfa.name: New Julfa
new-julfa.summary: The Armenian quarter of Isfahan, Iran, established in the early 17th century and named after the older city of Julfa; still one of the largest Armenian quarters in the world.

treaty-of-zuhab.name: Treaty of Zuhab
treaty-of-zuhab.summary: Treaty signed on 17 May 1639 ending the Ottoman-Safavid War of 1623 to 1639 and fixing borders between the two empires that closely resemble today's Turkey-Iran and Iraq-Iran borders.

simeon-of-poland.name: Simeon of Poland
simeon-of-poland.summary: Polish-Armenian traveler (1584–1639) known for his travelogue of a journey across the Ottoman domains and Italy from 1608 to 1619.

celali-rebellions.name: Celali rebellions
celali-rebellions.summary: A series of rebellions in Anatolia by irregular troops led by bandit chiefs against the Ottoman Empire, in the late 16th and early to mid-17th centuries.

tokat.name: Tokat
tokat.summary: A city in the mid-Black Sea region of Anatolia, Turkey, located where the Tokat River meets the Yeşilırmak.

sivas.name: Sivas
sivas.summary: A city in central Turkey with a population of about 365,000, historically a trade and manufacturing centre and a hub for railways and trade routes to Iraq and Iran.

selim-i.name: Selim I
selim-i.summary: Ottoman sultan from 1512 to 1520, known as Selim the Grim, whose conquest of the Mamluk Sultanate of Egypt and the Levant made the Ottoman Empire the leading Muslim power.

tabriz.name: Tabriz
tabriz.summary: A city in northwestern Iran and capital of East Azerbaijan province, historically also known as Tauris, noted today for its handicrafts and carpet weaving.

janissary.name: Janissaries
janissary.summary: Elite Ottoman infantry corps, among the first standing armies equipped mainly with firearms, recruited as boys from Christian families and converted to Islam; the corps was disbanded in 1826.

kartli.name: Kartli
kartli.summary: A historical region in central-to-eastern Georgia along the Mtkvari river, known to classical authors as Hiberia; it became a separate kingdom centered on Tbilisi after Georgia's 15th-century partition.

kakheti.name: Kakheti
kakheti.summary: A region of Georgia centered on Telavi, known as one of the country's most important wine-producing areas and home to sites like Gremi and Alaverdi Monastery.

teimuraz-i.name: Teimuraz I
teimuraz-i.summary: Georgian king who ruled Kakheti (1606–1648) and briefly Kartli (1625–1633), spending decades resisting Safavid Iranian domination before dying as the Shah's prisoner; also a noted poet.

rostom-of-kartli.name: Rostom Khan
rostom-of-kartli.summary: A Georgian Bagrationi prince (1565–1658) who rose to prominence in Safavid Persia and, appointed by the Shah, became king of Kartli from 1633 and of Kakheti from 1648.

imereti.name: Imereti
imereti.summary: A region of central-western Georgia along the Rioni River, the country's most populous region, centered on the city of Kutaisi.

karacao-lan.name: Karacaoğlan
karacao-lan.summary: A 17th-century Anatolian Turkish folk poet, born around 1606 and died around 1679, whose vivid poetry on nature and village life became a major influence on modern Turkish lyric poetry.

ottoman-turkish.name: Ottoman Turkish
ottoman-turkish.summary: The standardized Turkish language register used in the Ottoman Empire from the 14th to 20th centuries, borrowing heavily from Persian and Arabic and largely unintelligible to rural Turks.

tanzimat.name: Tanzimat
tanzimat.summary: A period of reforms in the Ottoman Empire from 1839 to 1876 that modernized legal, military and administrative systems.

ghazal.name: Ghazal
ghazal.summary: Poetic form originating in 7th-century Arabic poetry that deals with love and loss, later flourishing in Persian poetry and spreading across South Asia and Turkey.

qasida.name: Qasida
qasida.summary: An ancient Arabic ode form using a single meter and rhyme throughout, originating in pre-Islamic poetry and later adopted into Persian and Turkish literature.

bagrationi-dynasty.name: Bagrationi dynasty
bagrationi-dynasty.summary: A royal family that ruled Georgia from the Middle Ages to the early 19th century, among the oldest surviving Christian ruling dynasties in the world.

ukurova.name: Çukurova
ukurova.summary: A large fertile plain in the Cilicia region of southern Anatolia, also called the Cilician Plain, spanning parts of several Turkish provinces.

louis-xv.name: Louis XV
louis-xv.summary: King of France from 1715 to 1774, whose nearly 59-year reign saw the loss of New France and is generally judged by historians to have weakened the country.

kingdom-of-kakheti.name: Kingdom of Kakheti
kingdom-of-kakheti.summary: A late medieval and early modern monarchy in eastern Georgia, capital first at Gremi then Telavi, formed in 1466 from a division of the Kingdom of Georgia and lasting until merging with Kartli in 1762.

kahramanmara.name: Maraş
kahramanmara.summary: Historic name of the city now called Kahramanmaraş, in the Mediterranean region of Turkey, renamed in 1973 to commemorate the Battle of Marash.

matchlock.name: Matchlock (tüfenk)
matchlock.summary: A historical firearm fired by a burning cord that ignites the gunpowder via a trigger, an advance over the hand cannon that let the user aim without losing concentration.

murad-ii.name: Murad II
murad-ii.summary: Ottoman sultan who ruled twice, from 1421 to 1444 and again from 1446 to 1451.

miquelet-lock.name: Miquelet lock
miquelet-lock.summary: A type of flint-against-steel firing mechanism for muskets and pistols, used from the late 16th to mid-19th century across the Ottoman, Spanish and Portuguese empires and beyond.

battle-of-moh-cs.name: Battle of Mohács
battle-of-moh-cs.summary: A 29 August 1526 battle in which the Ottomans under Suleiman the Magnificent decisively defeated Hungary's King Louis II, ending the Jagiellonian dynasty there and leading to Hungary's partition.

bayezid-ii.name: Bayezid II
bayezid-ii.summary: Ottoman sultan from 1481 to 1512 who consolidated the empire and resettled Sephardi Jews expelled from Spain throughout Ottoman lands.

belgrade-fortress.name: Belgrade Fortress
belgrade-fortress.summary: A citadel and park at the meeting of the Sava and Danube rivers in Belgrade, forming the historic core of the city and one of Serbia's most visited sites.

millet-ottoman-empire.name: Millet
millet-ottoman-empire.summary: In the Ottoman Empire, an autonomous legal community allowing non-Muslim religious groups to govern themselves under their own laws, later used from the 19th century for protected ethnic minority groups.

halakha.name: Halakha
halakha.summary: The collective body of Jewish religious law derived from the Torah and later rabbinic writings, guiding both religious practice and everyday civil life.

safavid-dynasty.name: Safavid dynasty
safavid-dynasty.summary: Ruling dynasty of Safavid Iran from 1501 to 1736, of Kurdish origin based in Ardabil; Shah Ismail I made Twelver Shi'ism the state religion, a turning point in Islamic history.

rum-millet.name: Rum Millet
rum-millet.summary: The Ottoman Empire's Eastern Orthodox Christian community, encompassing Greeks, Bulgarians, Albanians, Georgians, Serbs and others, which retained a degree of internal autonomy.

ethnarch.name: Ethnarch
ethnarch.summary: A title meaning leadership over an ethnic or national group, from Greek words for "nation" and "ruler"; used for governors of a district, such as heads of Ottoman millet communities.

murad-iv.name: Murad IV
murad-iv.summary: Ottoman sultan from 1623 to 1640, known for restoring state authority through harsh methods and for an Ottoman-Safavid war that helped shape the modern Turkey-Iran-Iraq borders.

ottoman-safavid-war-1578-1590.name: Ottoman–Safavid War (1578–1590)
ottoman-safavid-war-1578-1590.summary: Conflict from 1577–78 to 1590 between the Ottoman and Safavid empires, exploiting Safavid succession chaos after Shah Tahmasp I's death; ended in an Ottoman victory after a 1583 turning point.

ottoman-safavid-war-1603-1612.name: Ottoman–Safavid War (1603–1612)
ottoman-safavid-war-1603-1612.summary: Conflict fought from 1603 to 1612 between Safavid Iran under Shah Abbas I and the Ottoman Empire, ending in a Safavid victory that restored their control over the Caucasus and western Iran.

ecumenical-patriarch-of-constantinople.name: Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople
ecumenical-patriarch-of-constantinople.summary: The archbishop of Constantinople and spiritual leader of Eastern Orthodox Christians worldwide, regarded as first among equals among Orthodox church heads.

treaty-of-k-k-kaynarca.name: Treaty of Küçük Kaynarca
treaty-of-k-k-kaynarca.summary: Ended the Russo-Turkish War of 1768–74 with major concessions to Russia, including effective control of the Crimean Khanate; historians see it as a milestone in Ottoman decline.

mehmed-ii.name: Mehmed II
mehmed-ii.summary: Ottoman sultan (1432–1481), known as the Conqueror, who captured Constantinople in 1453, ending the Byzantine Empire, and expanded Ottoman rule across Anatolia and the Balkans.

osman-ii.name: Osman II
osman-ii.summary: Ottoman sultan, also called Osman the Young, who ruled from 1618 until he was killed in a palace coup in 1622, aged 17.

halil-i-nalc-k.name: Halil İnalcık
halil-i-nalc-k.summary: A Turkish historian (1916–2016) whose influential research focused on the social and economic history of the Ottoman Empire, teaching at Ankara University, the University of Chicago and Bilkent University.

dariusz-ko-odziejczyk.name: Dariusz Kołodziejczyk
dariusz-ko-odziejczyk.summary: Polish historian and professor at the University of Warsaw specializing in the diplomatic history of Poland and the Ottoman Empire.

beylerbey.name: beylerbey
beylerbey.summary: High rank in the western Islamic world, from the Anatolian Seljuks and Ilkhanids to Safavid Iran and the Ottoman Empire, originally meaning commander-in-chief and later designating senior provincial governors-general.

imperial-council-ottoman-empire.name: Imperial Council
imperial-council-ottoman-empire.summary: De facto cabinet of the Ottoman Empire, chaired by the Grand Vizier and meeting in Topkapi Palace; its main executive power lasted until the mid-17th century.

vizier.name: Vizier
vizier.summary: High-ranking political advisor or minister historically used across greater Persia and later much of West Asia, South Asia and North Africa; the Abbasid caliphs first gave the title to a chief secretary.

eyalet.name: Eyalet
eyalet.summary: A major administrative province of the Ottoman Empire from 1453 until the early 19th century, governed by a beylerbey with broad military, financial and judicial powers.

zulfiqar.name: Zulfiqar
zulfiqar.summary: The legendary double-edged sword of Ali, cousin and son-in-law of Muhammad, closely associated with his bravery and later a widely used Islamic symbol.

little-ice-age.name: Little Ice Age
little-ice-age.summary: A period of regional cooling, mainly in the North Atlantic, usually dated from the 16th to 19th centuries or as early as 1300, with proposed causes including solar and volcanic activity.

arakel-of-tabriz.name: Arakel of Tabriz
arakel-of-tabriz.summary: Armenian historian and clergyman (1590s–1670) whose History is a key source on the Safavid and Ottoman empires, Armenia, Azerbaijan and Georgia from 1602 to 1662.

tahmasp-i.name: Tahmasp I
tahmasp-i.summary: Second shah of Safavid Iran, ruling from 1524 to 1576, who fought long wars with the Ottomans and Uzbeks and was a noted patron of painters, calligraphers and poets.

waqf.name: Waqf
waqf.summary: An inalienable charitable endowment under Islamic law, typically land or property donated for religious purposes and managed by a trustee, with its full legal form dating to the 9th century CE.

armenian-patriarchate-of-jerusalem.name: Armenian Patriarch of Jerusalem
armenian-patriarchate-of-jerusalem.summary: Head of the Armenian Patriarchate of Jerusalem, based in the Armenian Quarter of the Old City, overseeing the local Armenian community with a synod of clergy.

kuru.name: Kuruş
kuru.summary: A currency denomination used across former Ottoman territories, known in Europe as the piastre; today it survives as a subunit of the Turkish lira.
